title: SRO Tactics + Cards: the checks I use before sharing an AI-assisted build
author: Substantial-Book5072
selftext:
I'm building SRO Tactics and SRO Cards, two free browser fan games inspired by Silkroad Online. I use AI assistants for code and media preparation. The most useful change to my workflow has been giving a capture task the same release boundary as a code task.



For development, I split work into small file sets, use isolated working copies, then build and run targeted tests before merging. For screenshots, the instruction is equally specific: use the exact deployed build, run it locally with a throwaway guest state, keep the full HUD readable, and record the version, language and mode with the files. That keeps captures away from real player accounts and makes their source checkable later.



One concrete failure was a Roc boss screenshot with labels cut off on the right. It also looked like an isolated test board. I removed it from the showcase. For a later project introduction I used a normal Practice match capture. A generated caption or a successful capture command wouldn't have caught that. Opening the image at full size did.



Language needs its own check. My first Turkish-captioned teaser still had an English game interface, so I labelled that explicitly. The new capture actually uses the Turkish UI. Looking through it also exposed an English Critical popup and sound prompt; those are now tracked for translation. The image here is a local guest duel on the published 6q build, with the test-preview badge visible.



For video, I keep a contact sheet and decode the exported file, then play the uploaded version to the end. The new Cards clip joins three real sections: starting hand, a mana card and Movoi being played, then a later attack. I describe those cuts in the post. It doesn't show a completed duel. An earlier Tactics recording was only getting about one frame per second under development load, so I kept the stills. The later Cards recording was made when the machine was quieter.



Player testing still finds things these checks miss. One guest tester got a login message on the Story landing page despite working guest chapters, then a mana warning after the game had suggested ending the turn for a win. Both have local fixes awaiting release. The practical loop for me is specific report, reproduce, scoped change, tests, then check the actual screen again.



What checks do you put between an AI-assisted build and the first thing a new player sees? I'm interested in the small checks that have caught real mistakes for you.



Playable project: [https://www.srotactics.com/](https://www.srotactics.com/)

Both games are free, with guest access and no real-money purchases. Independent fan project, not affiliated with Joymax.
